e-5573.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
e-5573.problem:
Consider the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace $S=\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2 \},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068823/assets/bc9289885d7d9db73bedf7486b311cf7333ea0cb72520ce3399a9b15f2c9b4c8.png)

Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ is orthogonal.
e-5573.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} 
= \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{a}_1}\mathbf{x} + \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{a}_2}\mathbf{x}.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1\}$ and $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_2\}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{2\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=1[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{2\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 1}{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+(-\frac{1}{2})[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-7173.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
e-7173.problem:
Consider the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the plane $\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{v}+t\mathbf{w},$ where $s,t\in\mathbb R,$ and
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068823/assets/11a1a4da746f8286edde9e12f17a7eaae9f4a242dfdab8ed137674c2d8e0c04c.png) 
Find the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the plane given that $\mathbf{v} \perp \mathbf{w}.$
e-7173.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^3.$ 
And, since the set $\{\mathbf{v},\mathbf{w}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by   

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} = \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{v}}\,\mathbf{x} + \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{w}}\,\mathbf{x}.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{v}\}$ and $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{w}\}\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{13\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 3+(-1)\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}v=\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{13\cdot 5+(-2)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 1}{{5}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=2[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ \frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ -\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-5574.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Vector and a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
e-5574.problem:
Consider the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace $S=\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2 \},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068823/assets/7e767fa1b102062adfe30a12660ee0854ecd14829cd158160e95c9efbcc718b5.png)

Find the distance between $\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ is orthogonal.
e-5574.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} 
= \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{a}_1}\mathbf{x} + \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{a}_2}\mathbf{x}.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1\}$ and $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_2\}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot 2+1\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(3-2)}^{2}+{(2-2)}^{2}+{(1-2)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -3 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{12\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 0+9\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{12\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 1+9\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$

$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}12 \\ -3 \\ 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
content.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{12\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 0+9\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{12\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 1+9\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 2 \\ 10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Consider the vector x and the subspace S=Span{a1,a2,a3}, where a1=[1102],a2=[3−501],a3=[1150−8],x=[463−17]. Find the orthogonal projection of x onto the subspace S given that the set {a1,a2,a3} is orthogonal.

a
[460−17]
b
[403−17]
c
[063−17]
d
[−6400]
e
[4600]
Submit

decision.explanation: Using the orthogonal basis, proj_S(x) = Σ (x·aᵢ)/(aᵢ·aᵢ)aᵢ. The coefficients are -24/6 = -4, -35/35 = -1, and 210/210 = 1. Thus proj_S(x) = -4a₁ - a₂ + a₃ = (4,6,0,-17), which is option a.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ 3 \\ -17\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4\cdot 1+6\cdot 1+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{1}=-\frac{24}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{4\cdot 3+6\cdot (-5)+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{35}{35}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{4\cdot 11+6\cdot 5+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot (-8)}{{11}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{210}{210}[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ 0 \\ -17\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ 3 \\ -17\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
content.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4\cdot 1+6\cdot 1+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{1}=-\frac{24}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{4\cdot 3+6\cdot (-5)+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{35}{35}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{4\cdot 11+6\cdot 5+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot (-8)}{{11}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{210}{210}[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ 0 \\ -17\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -20 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{20\cdot 4+(-20)\cdot 5+0\cdot 0}{{4}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=-\frac{20}{41}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{20\cdot 5+(-20)\cdot (-4)+0\cdot 0}{{5}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{180}{41}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =-\frac{20}{41}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{180}{41}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{20}{41}(-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+9[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -20 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** The projection is the vector $x$ itself. This means that $x$ can be written as a linear combination of ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$ In other words, $x$ lies in the subspace spanned by ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}.$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set 
${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot 2+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 1+4\cdot (-4)+3\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set 
${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
content.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot 2+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 1+4\cdot (-4)+3\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 5
before.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.

decision.explanation: The orthogonal-basis projection coefficients are 7/4, 11/12, and -4/6 = -2/3. Therefore proj_S(x) = (7/4)a₁ + (11/12)a₂ − (2/3)a₃ = (1,4,2,2), option e. The residual (0,0,1,-1) is orthogonal to all three basis vectors.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot (-1)+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 3+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{1\cdot 0+4\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(21[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+11[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
content.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot (-1)+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 3+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{1\cdot 0+4\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(21[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+11[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
after.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-2)\cdot (-3)+(-2)\cdot 2+(-9)\cdot 1}{(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-2)\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 2+(-9)\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}w=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace S=Span{v,w} in R3. And, since the set {v,w} is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of x onto the subspace S is given by

projSx=projvx+projwx.

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of x onto Span{a1} and Span{a2}:

projvx=x⋅vv⋅vv=(−2)⋅(−3)+(−2)⋅2+(−9)⋅1(−3)2+22+12v=−12[−321]projwx=x⋅ww⋅ww=(−2)⋅1+(−2)⋅2+(−9)⋅(−1)12+22+(−1)2w=12[12−1]

Therefore, we have that projSx=projvx+projwx=−12[−321]+12[12−1]=12(−[−321]+[12−1])=[20−1].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
content.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-2)\cdot (-3)+(-2)\cdot 2+(-9)\cdot 1}{(-3)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-2)\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot 2+(-9)\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}w=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 14 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
after.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-8)\cdot 4+14\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 2}{{4}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}v=-2[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-8)\cdot 1+14\cdot 2+2\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}w=3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 2 \\ -4\text{ }\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

projvx=x⋅vv⋅vv=(−8)⋅4+14⋅(−1)+2⋅242+(−1)2+22v=−2[4−12]=[−82−4]projwx=x⋅ww⋅ww=(−8)⋅1+14⋅2+2⋅(−1)12+22+(−1)2w=3[12−1]=[36−3]

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms the projection is -2v + 3w = (-5,8,-7), option e. The residual (-3,6,9) has zero dot product with both v and w, independently verifying the result. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option a.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 14 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
content.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-8)\cdot 4+14\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 2}{{4}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}v=-2[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-8)\cdot 1+14\cdot 2+2\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}w=3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 2 \\ -4\text{ }\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector x and the plane r=sv+tw, where s,t∈R, and v=[3−41],w=[541],x=[−3−1117]. Find the orthogonal projection of x onto the plane given that v⊥w.

a
[3−31]
b
[−1124]
c
[12−212]
d
[1121]
e
[1−121]
Submit

decision.explanation: Since v and w are orthogonal, the projection is (x·v)/(v·v)v + (x·w)/(w·w)w. The coefficients are 52/26 = 2 and -42/42 = -1, so the projection is 2v − w = (1,-12,1), option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -11 \\ 17\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
after.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-3)\cdot 3+(-11)\cdot (-4)+17\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-3)\cdot 5+(-11)\cdot 4+17\cdot 1}{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -12 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8

Consider the vector x and the plane r=sv+tw, where s,t∈R, and v=[3−41],w=[541],x=[−3−1117]. Find the orthogonal projection of x onto the plane given that v⊥w.

a
[3−31]
b
[−1124]
c
[12−212]
d
[1121]
e
[1−121]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace S=Span{v,w} in R3. And, since the set {v,w} is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of x onto the subspace S is given by

projSx=projvx+projwx.

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of x onto Span{a1} and Span{a2}:

projvx=x⋅vv⋅vv=(−3)⋅3+(−11)⋅(−4)+17⋅132+(−4)2+12v=[6−82]projwx=x⋅ww⋅ww=(−3)⋅5+(−11)⋅4+17⋅152+42+12w=[−5−4−1]

Therefore, we have that projSx=projvx+projwx=[6−82]+[−5−4−1]=[1−121].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -11 \\ 17\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
content.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-3)\cdot 3+(-11)\cdot (-4)+17\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-3)\cdot 5+(-11)\cdot 4+17\cdot 1}{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -8 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -12 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -12\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
content.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{15\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot 6+(-3)\cdot (-12)}{{3}^{2}+{6}^{2}+(-12)^{2}}v=\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ -12\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{15\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}w=4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ 6 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the vector x and the plane r=sv+tw, where s,t∈R, and v=[4−42],w=[32−2],x=[−9231]. Find the orthogonal projection of x onto the plane given that v⊥w.

a
[−10−1112]
b
[−13−1211]
c
 [−13−1415]
d
[−11−1213]
e
 [−12−1110]
Submit

decision.explanation: Since v and w are orthogonal, the projection is (x·v)/(v·v)v + (x·w)/(w·w)w = (18/36)v − (85/17)w = v/2 − 5w = (-13,-12,11), option b.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 2 \\ 31\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
after.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-9)\cdot 4+2\cdot (-4)+31\cdot 2}{{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}}v=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-9)\cdot 3+2\cdot 2+31\cdot (-2)}{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}w=-5[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ -10 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-13 \\ -12 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the vector x and the plane r=sv+tw, where s,t∈R, and v=[4−42],w=[32−2],x=[−9231]. Find the orthogonal projection of x onto the plane given that v⊥w.

a
[−10−1112]
b
[−13−1211]
c
 [−13−1415]
d
[−11−1213]
e
 [−12−1110]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace S=Span{v,w} in R3. And, since the set {v,w} is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of x onto the subspace S is given by

projSx=projvx+projwx.

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of x onto Span{a1} and Span{a2}:

projvx=x⋅vv⋅vv=(−9)⋅4+2⋅(−4)+31⋅242+(−4)2+22v=12[4−42]projwx=x⋅ww⋅ww=(−9)⋅3+2⋅2+31⋅(−2)32+22+(−2)2w=−5[32−2]

Therefore, we have that projSx=projvx+projwx=12[4−42]−5[32−2]=[2−21]+[−15−1010]=[−13−1211].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 2 \\ 31\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
content.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-9)\cdot 4+2\cdot (-4)+31\cdot 2}{{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}}v=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-9)\cdot 3+2\cdot 2+31\cdot (-2)}{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}w=-5[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ -10 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-13 \\ -12 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Consider the vector x and the subspace S=Span{a1,a2} where a1=[3−10],a2=[130],x=[30−3]. Find the distance between x and the subspace S given that the set {a1,a2} is orthogonal.

a
9
b
3
c
93
d
0
e
27
Submit

decision.explanation: The two nonzero orthogonal vectors span the xy-plane. Thus the projection of x is (3,0,0), and the distance is the norm of the residual (0,0,-3), which equals 3.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
after.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{3\cdot 3+0\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 0}{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{9}{10}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3\cdot 1+0\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{9}{10}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{3}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{3}{10}([\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-3)^{2}+(0-0)^{2}+(-3-0)^{2}} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Vector and a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
content.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
content.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{3\cdot 3+0\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 0}{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{9}{10}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3\cdot 1+0\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{9}{10}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{3}{10}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{3}{10}([\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(3-3)^{2}+(0-0)^{2}+(-3-0)^{2}} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
